skill.name: swarm-advanced
skill.description: Advanced guidance for coordinating Claude Flow swarms across research, development, testing, and analysis workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate specialized AI agents for parallel research, coding, testing, analysis, and workflow automation.
skill.author: Claude Flow Team

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code fences, inline skill names, or documentation links rather than executable Ruby backticks. Confirmed risks are limited to bash examples that ask users to install or run Claude Flow through npm or npx. No prompt injection, hidden data exfiltration, or hostile intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Quick start commands install and run third-party package code.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a stable Claude Flow version, explain the trust boundary, and require user confirmation before running npm or npx commands.

remediation.issue: CLI fallback examples may be copied or executed by agents without enough context.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit approval language before CLI fallback blocks and prefer MCP tool calls when available.

content.value_statement: Complex AI work can become slow when one agent handles every task. This skill shows how to coordinate specialized swarms for research, development, testing, and analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains mesh, hierarchical, star, and ring swarm topologies.
Provides research, development, testing, and analysis swarm patterns.
Shows MCP tool sequences for agent spawning, memory, monitoring, and task orchestration.
Includes CLI fallback examples for Claude Flow swarm workflows.
Covers fault tolerance, state management, workflow automation, and performance monitoring.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow tools or CLI support to execute examples.
Does not verify that referenced packages or MCP servers are safe.
Examples need adaptation before use in production repositories.
Does not replace human review of agent actions and generated outputs.

use_cases.title: Plan Parallel Research
use_cases.description: Use a mesh swarm to gather sources, validate evidence, analyze patterns, and produce a structured report.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Use a hierarchical swarm to split architecture, backend, frontend, testing, review, and documentation work.

use_cases.title: Run Quality Workflows
use_cases.description: Use a star swarm to coordinate unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and security testing.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Topology
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to recommend a topology for this task: [describe task]. Explain the agent roles and execution order.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Research Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to design a research swarm for [topic]. Include agent roles, phases, validation steps, and final deliverables.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Development Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to plan a development swarm for [feature]. Include architecture, implementation, testing, review, documentation, and monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Running Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to diagnose this swarm issue: [symptoms]. Recommend topology changes, recovery steps, metrics, and memory strategy.

output_examples.input: Plan a research swarm for evaluating AI governance trends.
output_examples.output: Recommended topology: mesh. Suggested roles: web researcher, academic researcher, data analyst, pattern analyst, and report writer. The workflow gathers sources, validates quality, identifies trends, and produces a final report.

output_examples.input: Create a development swarm for a REST API with authentication.
output_examples.output: Recommended topology: hierarchical. Suggested roles: architect, backend developer, database engineer, QA engineer, security reviewer, and technical writer. The workflow moves from design to parallel implementation, testing, review, and release notes.
Recommended actions: reduce overlapping test roles, separate dependent tests from independent tests, collect runtime metrics, and adjust agent count based on bottlenecks.

best_practices: Choose the topology from task dependencies, not from team size alone.
Assign each agent a clear role, capability set, and expected deliverable.
Monitor swarm health, memory usage, and task results during long workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not run large swarms without a clear coordinator or task plan.
Do not let multiple agents own the same deliverable without review rules.
Do not run CLI fallback commands without confirming package trust and user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you design and operate coordinated AI agent swarms for complex research, coding, testing, and analysis work.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Flow?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples are built around Claude Flow MCP tools and CLI workflows.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the planning guidance, but execution depends on available tools in the workspace.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: It is an advanced skill. Beginners should start with topology selection and small swarms before using automation patterns.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill is documentation, but it includes CLI examples that users or agents may execute if approved.

faq.question: How should I use it safely?
faq.answer: Review external commands, verify package sources, limit agent permissions, and inspect outputs before applying changes.
